subject: Post-contract usage adjustment & one-time invoice patch
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-contract usage adjustment & one-time invoice patch

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. We dug into the June traffic you flagged and confirmed there was a short-lived but material increase in inference hours that occurred after the renewal cutover on 6/10. The spike looks like an automated batch job that started hitting a new endpoint and ran across multiple service nodes.

Summary (quick):
- Delta usage (6/10–6/30): 1.2M inference minutes above committed baseline
- Estimated incremental charge (raw): $12,500
- Root cause: stray workload routing + retry storm during deployment

Our proposal to keep this clean and avoid procurement churn:
1) Issue a one-time invoice for the raw overage, then apply a courtesy credit to reduce the total.
2) Offer to amortize the remaining balance across your next three monthly statements if that helps cashflow.
3) Add a short-term commit top-up (if you want) to prevent repeat spikes while you validate the fix.

I've attached the usage export and a draft invoice for your review: usage-report-June2026.csv, proposed-invoice-12345.pdf.

Could you confirm whether Novus prefers (A) a single reduced invoice we send now, or (B) the amortized path across Q3 invoices? If you prefer (B) we can issue a smaller immediate invoice and push credits on the next three cycles.

Would love to close this off by EOD Thursday so finance can lock the numbers before month-end.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0179

Thanks, Mina. Appreciate the quick analysis and the proposed paths. A couple of notes from procurement / finance on our side:  

- We'd prefer to avoid a single large invoice hitting our July P&L. Amortizing over three months would be preferable (option B).
- Can you remove any late/penalty fees — this was clearly a deployment issue tied to the cutover.
- Please provide an itemized breakdown (raw hours, unit rate, credits applied) we can send to our AP team.

If you can send an updated invoice that breaks out the numbers and shows the amortization schedule, procurement can sign off quickly. We may also request that you apply a one-time operational goodwill credit (we're asking for 30% off the overage before amortization). Is that something you can approve?

Appreciate it — Alicia

Team — forwarding Alicia's ask. Key points: Novus prefers amortization (3 months) and is requesting a 30% one-time goodwill credit before amortization. They also want a fully itemized breakdown for AP.

Suggested resolution (my recommendation):
- Approve a 30% courtesy credit on the delta usage ($12,500 -> credit $3,750), leaving $8,750 to bill.
- Issue an immediate invoice for $2,917 (one-third) and place $2,917 credits on the next two invoices, or alternately, we can issue a $8,750 invoice and apply credits over the next three invoices at our end (whichever is simpler for finance).
- No late fees. We absorb the penalty given the deployment-related origin and the customer is an expansion win (DEAL-7391).

Ben — can you confirm if RevOps is okay with the 30% courtesy write-down? If yes, please generate final invoice number and routing. Marissa — can CS help confirm the remediation notes and the short-term top-up suggestion for next month? I want to close this with procurement by EOD Thursday.

Thanks — Mina

Alicia — thanks for the quick turnaround. RevOps signed off on the courtesy reduction (Ben confirmed) and we've prepared the final schedule below.

Agreed settlement:
- Raw overage: $12,500
- One-time courtesy credit (approved): 30% = $3,750
- Net amount to collect: $8,750
- Amortization: three equal postings of $2,917 across July/August/September invoices (first posting is the immediate invoice)
- No late/penalty fees applied

What we are sending you now:
- Final invoice (final-invoice-12345.pdf) reflecting the above and the amortization schedule.
- DocuSign link for the settlement addendum: https://www.docusign.com/sign/xyz-7492

If procurement signs the addendum, finance will issue the first invoice today and schedule the credits for subsequent invoices. Marissa will also follow up with a short remediation note describing the fix we applied to routing rules to prevent recurrence.

Thanks again for working through this quickly — please let me know once procurement has countersigned the DocuSign and I'll confirm the invoice number.
